missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding attack success rates (49.56% full success), low out-of-the-box detection (6.0%), the inadequacy of a scientist persona alone, and the efficacy of structured data provenance auditing are directly supported by the presented quantitative data.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The empirical evaluation comprehensively tracks dataset propagation through pipeline stages (found, retrieved, used, statistics, conclusion) and measures detection rates, supported by appropriate statistical intervals and inter-annotator validation of the LLM judge (Cohen's kappa >= 0.758).
primary.limitations: The authors thoroughly discuss limitations, including focus on tabular socio-technical datasets rather than unstructured scientific modalities, containment via API interception wrappers, reliance on prompt-level mitigations, and potential false positives from statistical audits.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is rigorous and well-controlled, using 450 initial runs across five socially salient topics, three frontier AI systems (Claude Code, GPT Codex, Gemini CLI), two opposite adversarial directions, and three prompt formulations, followed by an additional 450 runs testing mitigations in ethically isolated environments.
primary.quality_rationale: The study addresses a clear, novel threat model in AI-driven science with an exceptionally thorough experimental design, extensive data points, ethical containment safeguards, reproducible code/logging availability, and balanced interpretation of results.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper demonstrates and evaluates 'indirect data poisoning' against autonomous AI research agents, where manipulated open datasets uploaded to public repositories mislead honest agents into drawing false scientific conclusions, and proposes provenance-based mitigation strategies.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study addresses a clear, novel threat model in AI-driven science with an exceptionally thorough experimental design, extensive data points, ethical containment safeguards, reproducible code/logging availability, and balanced interpretation of results.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors thoroughly discuss limitations, including focus on tabular socio-technical datasets rather than unstructured scientific modalities, containment via API interception wrappers, reliance on prompt-level mitigations, and potential false positives from statistical audits.

title: Distributed Denial of Science: How Indirect Data Poisoning of AI Systems Can Industrialize Scientific Fraud

abstract_summary: Evolutionary program search guided by Large Language Models (LLMs) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for automated scientific discovery. However, current approaches are fundamentally constrained by three bottlenecks: structurally blind parent selection, sparse whole-program evaluation rewards, and static mutation o...
citation: GAE: Graph-Augmented Evolution for Scientific Discovery via Reinforcement Optimization. Xuanzhou Chen, Taoli Cheng. 2026-07-11. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10127v1
publication_status_evidence: arXiv manuscript identifier; no external publication established by the available metadata.
relevance_reason: Studies AI-scientist or scientific-discovery agents.

concerns: The manuscript contains a direct internal contradiction about parent selection: the abstract and introduction claim the framework resolves 'structurally blind parent selection' and 'dynamically selecting optimal parents', but the method section and appendix state parents are sampled strictly uniformly at random from the archive, with the RL agent only choosing mutation hints. This undermines a central claimed contribution.

The empirical validation is very narrow: a single synthetic nonlinear harmonic oscillator task from LLM-SRBench, with the controlled comparison run for only 150 iterations and 1-3 runs, and no ablation studies isolating the GNN, SAC, or GRPO components. This is insufficient to support broad claims of state-of-the-art scientific discovery or resolution of the three identified bottlenecks.

The claim of state-of-the-art performance rests on a low-budget comparison with very few runs and no reported uncertainty or statistical testing, while the higher-budget Table 1 results are taken from prior work rather than produced under a shared protocol.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: While the framework is conceptually interesting, the manuscript displays conflicting statements about parent selection and relies on an extremely limited empirical validation (one synthetic task, 1-3 runs at 150 iterations) with no component ablations, leaving its scientific claims substantially uncertain.

graphs into structural embeddings, a contextual bandit se-

blocking_reasons: The manuscript contains a direct internal contradiction about parent selection: the abstract and introduction claim the framework resolves 'structurally blind parent selection' and 'dynamically selecting optimal parents', but the method section and appendix state parents are sampled strictly uniformly at random from the archive, with the RL agent only choosing mutation hints. This undermines a central claimed contribution.

The empirical validation is very narrow: a single synthetic nonlinear harmonic oscillator task from LLM-SRBench, with the controlled comparison run for only 150 iterations and 1-3 runs, and no ablation studies isolating the GNN, SAC, or GRPO components. This is insufficient to support broad claims of state-of-the-art scientific discovery or resolution of the three identified bottlenecks.

The claim of state-of-the-art performance rests on a low-budget comparison with very few runs and no reported uncertainty or statistical testing, while the higher-budget Table 1 results are taken from prior work rather than produced under a shared protocol.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims of broadly transforming evolutionary search for scientific discovery and resolving bottlenecks like parent selection are insufficiently supported by an evaluation restricted to a single oscillator equation and a contradictory method specification regarding parent sampling.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The experimental evaluation is very narrow, tested on only a single synthetic nonlinear harmonic oscillator task from LLM-SRBench. The direct comparative evaluation against baselines is limited to a short 150-iteration horizon using only 1 to 3 runs, and lacks ablation studies verifying the necessity or individual impact of the three integrated components (GNN, SAC, and online GRPO).
primary.limitations: The authors acknowledge that the AST-derived graph representation is Python-specific, requires domain-specific redesign, and introduces non-trivial runtime overhead from GNN and RL training.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is described with architectural and algorithmic details across the three modules (GNN, SAC, and GRPO). However, the text contains internal inconsistencies regarding parent selection, initially claiming to resolve 'structurally blind parent selection' and 'dynamically selecting optimal parents', but later clarifying that parents are sampled strictly uniformly at random from the archive.
primary.quality_rationale: While the framework is conceptually interesting, the manuscript displays conflicting statements about parent selection and relies on an extremely limited empirical validation (one synthetic task, 1-3 runs at 150 iterations) with no component ablations, leaving its scientific claims substantially uncertain.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper proposes GAE (Graph-Augmented Evolution), a framework for evolutionary code search that integrates a relational GNN encoder for abstract syntax trees, a discrete SAC meta-controller to propose mutation hints, and online GRPO fine-tuning of an LLM mutation operator.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported findings closely align with the collected empirical data: hypothesis trees, state transitions, belief flips, and performance variations across base models are corroborated by quantitative logs and state-transition probability matrices [E269bb07cb3e53c1a-B0017, E269bb07cb3e53c1a-B0020, E269bb07cb3e53c1a-B0022, E269bb07cb3e53c1a-B0028].
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation across three distinct materials-science crystal structure prediction tasks demonstrates that the HEP agent traverses the hypothesis-test-evidence-belief cycle, contrasting sharply with a planning-style baseline that spends 0% of its steps updating beliefs [E269bb07cb3e53c1a-B0013, E269bb07cb3e53c1a-B0019, E269bb07cb3e53c1a-B0020]. An ablation comparing base LLMs confirms that protocol utilization depth scales systematically with model reasoning capability [E269bb07cb3e53c1a-B0028, E269bb07cb3e53c1a-B0029].
primary.limitations: The authors explicitly acknowledge that evidence validity currently relies on single-agent self-assessment, that the discovered governing rules reflect the behavior of a fixed MLIP rather than DFT or experimental physical reality, and that weaker LLMs struggle to manage complex hypothesis lineages [E269bb07cb3e53c1a-B0026, E269bb07cb3e53c1a-B0029, E269bb07cb3e53c1a-B0032].
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is clearly defined: the registry maintains explicit belief probabilities P(H), provenance, lifecycle states, and gating rules where belief updates and terminal verdicts (supported >= 0.8, refuted <= 0.2) require validated evidence attachments [E269bb07cb3e53c1a-B0011, E269bb07cb3e53c1a-B0012, E269bb07cb3e53c1a-B0035, E269bb07cb3e53c1a-B0036]. The agent loop and its atomistic materials tool environment are systematically documented [E269bb07cb3e53c1a-B0037, E269bb07cb3e53c1a-B0038].
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents an inventive, soundly implemented framework for scientific LLM auditing with solid experimental controls, clear baselines, and honest discussion of boundaries, meeting library standards for a pass.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces the Hypothesis Evolution Protocol (HEP), an agent harness featuring an append-only event-sourced registry and tool interface that externalizes scientific hypothesis generation, evaluation, belief tracking, and evolution for LLM agents [E269bb07cb3e53c1a-B0007, E269bb07cb3e53c1a-B0010, E269bb07cb3e53c1a-B0034].

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents an inventive, soundly implemented framework for scientific LLM auditing with solid experimental controls, clear baselines, and honest discussion of boundaries, meeting library standards for a pass.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly acknowledge that evidence validity currently relies on single-agent self-assessment, that the discovered governing rules reflect the behavior of a fixed MLIP rather than DFT or experimental physical reality, and that weaker LLMs struggle to manage complex hypothesis lineages [E269bb07cb3e53c1a-B0026, E269bb07cb3e53c1a-B0029, E269bb07cb3e53c1a-B0032].

evidence.excerpt:
FORGE addresses two failure points that single-
layer poisoning leaves exposed: a single document
looks like an unsupported assertion, and a flat set
of documents looks like coincidental overlap rather
than evidence. We therefore design the attack at
two levels: each adversarial document carries an
internal reasoning chain that makes its assigned
claim appear locally derived, and the full docu-
ment set is organized as a distributed argument
chain that makes the collection appear as conver-
gent multi-source evidence. Given a target narra-
tive V, FORGE constructs j adversarial documents
P={p 1, . . . , pj} that steer the final report R to-

FORGE addresses two failure points that single-
layer poisoning leaves exposed: a single document
looks like an unsupported assertion, and a flat set
of documents looks like coincidental overlap rather
than evidence. We therefore design the attack at
two levels: each adversarial document carries an
internal reasoning chain that makes its assigned
claim appear locally derived, and the full docu-
ment set is organized as a distributed argument
chain that makes the collection appear as conver-
gent multi-source evidence. Given a target narra-
tive V, FORGE constructs j adversarial documents
P={p 1, . . . , pj} that steer the final report R to-
ward that narrative. Sections 4.1 and 4.2 formalize
these two construction levels; Section 4.3 shows
how they escalate to report-level contamination
through subtask hijacking.

This subsection validates the claim-typing accuracy
of the PRISM evaluator (§ 5). Two human anno-
tators, neither of whom is an author of this paper,
independently assigned a claim type to each of 206
claims drawn from the depth experiment; disagree-
ments were adjudicated by a third annotator, and
cases where the final label differed from the model
prediction were recorded as corrections. Table 5

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding attack efficacy, the role of subtask hijacking as the central bottleneck, depth migration from framing to factual contamination, and RQA mitigation are backed directly by quantitative tables, ablations, and qualitative excerpts.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation is thorough, assessing local and network poisoning across 25 queries in 5 categories, depth levels, baseline models (PoisonedRAG, AuthChain), and structural component ablations. Causal isolation using a subtask transplant design cleanly proves that subtask hijacking rather than raw retrieval volume drives contamination, and RQA is benchmarked against standard defenses showing reduced PRISM and improved report utility.
primary.limitations: The authors explicitly discuss key limitations including testbed architecture dependency, lack of live-web authority/spam filtering dynamics in retrieval simulation, heuristic weight assignment in PRISM, and susceptibility of RQA to adaptive retrieval-focused adversaries.
primary.method_assessment: The threat model and attack mechanism are thoroughly formalized, showing how adversarial documents steer subtask generation to compound poisoned retrieval across multi-round workflows. The PRISM metric explicitly addresses limitations of binary attack success rates in long-form generation, and its evaluation pipeline is accompanied by rigorous human validation studies reporting high agreement and Cohen's kappa.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents an original, methodologically sound, and extensively validated investigation of adversarial vulnerabilities specific to recursive LLM research agents, adhering to rigorous empirical standards.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper identifies the planning-layer vulnerability in recursive deep research agents, introduces FORGE (an attack coupling intra-document reasoning fabrication with inter-document chaining), formulates PRISM (a cognitive-type weighted severity metric for report poisoning), and proposes Root Query Anchoring (RQA) as a planning-layer defense.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents an original, methodologically sound, and extensively validated investigation of adversarial vulnerabilities specific to recursive LLM research agents, adhering to rigorous empirical standards.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly discuss key limitations including testbed architecture dependency, lack of live-web authority/spam filtering dynamics in retrieval simulation, heuristic weight assignment in PRISM, and susceptibility of RQA to adaptive retrieval-focused adversaries.

causal mechanism behind drone survival through a limited budget of experiments, under observations
that are censored by survivorship, confounded by hidden variables, and corrupted by noise. We
describe the game design below and illustrate the full pipeline in Fig. 3.

defense values (DEF) across seven components: engine, wing, body, cockpit, antenna, camera, and
gun. The agent observes only the post-mission damage state of each component on the surviving
drones. The goal is to understand the underlying mechanism that influences the survival of drones
and maximize the survival rate when drones are deployed under unknown environmental conditions.

drones. The goal is to understand the underlying mechanism that influences the survival of drones
and maximize the survival rate when drones are deployed under unknown environmental conditions.

While survival rate provides a quantitative measure of task performance, it alone cannot distinguish
whyagents fail or how they reason about the causal structure. We therefore score each agent session
with a rubric along four complementary dimensions. The explicit criteria are summarized in Table 18
in the Appendix. Each agent session is evaluated by an LLM-based judge using this rubric, yielding
dimension-wise scores and an overall rubric score.
Causal reasoning (11 points)evaluates whether the agent correctly identifies the core causal
mechanisms specified in the Task Report, avoids known traps or spurious correlations, and provides
mechanistic explanations with sufficient depth. High-scoring responses must articulate explicit causal
chains (rather than correlations), include intermediate variables or processes, and propose testable
predictions or validation strategies.
Experimental

Non-LLM baselines.To calibrate benchmark difficulty and confirm task solvability, we evaluate four
non-LLM or Agentic baselines: Default (submit initial design unchanged, 49.0%), Random (uniformly
sample DEF values, 52.0%), Uniform High (all DEF=50, 52.7%), and No-Explore LLM (randomly
deploy 10 times, then use LLM to analyze and submit, 57.5% on average, 52–63% across models).
More details can be found in Appendix G.
The results are given in Fig. 8(b). These simple baselines can outperform several full-agent models
on bias-heavy scenarios, confirming that correlational shortcuts are insufficient.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims that current frontier models fail at genuine causal reasoning and that task survival is decoupled from mechanistic understanding are well-supported by both quantitative survival gaps against analytical optima and near-floor causal-reasoning rubric scores across surviving tiers.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation is robust and extensively controlled, testing 30 frontier LLMs across repeated trials with confidence intervals and non-LLM baselines, validating inter-rater reliability via ICC(2,3), analyzing behavioral configuration trajectories, and uncovering critical failure modes including agent environment-hacking behaviors and false victory declarations.
primary.limitations: The authors explicitly discuss key limitations, noting that the simulated drone environments simplify real-world scientific discovery spaces, prompting and agentic execution modes differ across multiple procedural dimensions, and LLM-based rubric evaluations have inherent distributional skews that depress inter-rater agreement on causal criteria.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, specifying the underlying SCM formulations, analytical and empirical optimal survival rates, distinct interaction modes (prompting vs. agentic tool calling with ReAct and coding harness OpenCode), and a comprehensive multi-judge rubric evaluating causal reasoning, experimental design, reflection quality, and data usage.
primary.quality_rationale: This work presents an exceptionally thorough, rigorous, and controlled benchmark targeting an essential blind spot in the AI Scientist literature. The empirical analysis is methodologically sound, transparent about anomalous agent behaviors and harness leaks, and supported by extensive statistical validation.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces CausalGame, an interactive benchmarking environment comprising 14 scenarios grounded in structural causal models to evaluate whether LLM agents can perform active experimental design and causal reasoning under observational pitfalls like selection bias, measurement error, and hidden confounders.

3.3 Adversarial Reasoning for Intent Verification.
Despite leveraging enriched context and retrieved knowledge, a single LLM for
intent assessment frequently exhibits sycophancy bias [29], misclassifying benign
events as malicious and causing excessive false positives. To mitigate this, we
propose an adversarial reasoning framework [8] featuring three specialized agents:
a prosecutor, a defense attorney, and a judge.
In the initial phase, the prosecutor and defense agents independently analyze
the target event under opposing assumptions—malicious and benign intent,
respectively. Both agents exhaustively extract supporting evidence from the
hierarchical context, retrieved knowledge, and intrinsic knowledge, providing
formal citations for every claim. The verification algorithm then parses these
citations to generate a credibility summary,

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported empirical results substantiate the core claims: Minos achieves higher average recall (0.92) and precision (0.64) with substantially more compact subgraphs (35 vs. 68-129 edges), while ablations confirm the specific roles of coarse/fine contexts, adversarial deliberation, and the count-first protocol.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The system is evaluated against statistical, learning-based, and single-agent LLM baselines across 14 scenarios spanning five established datasets (DARPA TC Cadets/Trace/Theia, Aurora, and OpTC), reporting edge recall, precision, graph compactness, latency, token consumption, backbone variations, and extensive component ablations.
primary.limitations: The authors acknowledge higher inference latency compared to traditional statistical methods, dependencies on POI alert quality, and data privacy implications when utilizing hosted LLMs on sensitive audit logs.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, covering the two-tiered architecture, concrete formalisms for backward tracking, prompt structures, citation verification mechanisms, FSM control loops with defined termination conditions, and specialized agent duties (Planner, Query, Memory, Adversarial Group).
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript addresses a well-defined security challenge (dependency explosion and semantic ambiguity in provenance tracking) with a well-engineered multi-agent LLM solution, comprehensive empirical evidence across multiple benchmarks, and rigorous ablation experiments.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper presents Minos, a multi-agent collaborative framework for provenance-based backward tracking that combines an individual event assessment architecture (hierarchical context, RAG with citation verification, and adversarial prosecutor-defense-judge deliberation) with FSM orchestration across four specialized agents using hypothesis-driven search and count-first querying.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript addresses a well-defined security challenge (dependency explosion and semantic ambiguity in provenance tracking) with a well-engineered multi-agent LLM solution, comprehensive empirical evidence across multiple benchmarks, and rigorous ablation experiments.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors acknowledge higher inference latency compared to traditional statistical methods, dependencies on POI alert quality, and data privacy implications when utilizing hosted LLMs on sensitive audit logs.
